context: Set the skeleton headline to the canonical loaded copy so the h1 is stable across loading and loaded states, then update the Vitest loading-state assertion that pins the retired string. This is the root-cause fix that makes heading assertions time-invariant.
description: PR #1482 renamed the loaded Home h1 to 'BenchBox Curated Results Preview' (Home.tsx ~352) but left HomeLoadingSkeleton's h1 as 'BenchBox Database Leaderboards' (~598, reached from the early return ~257). The retired string now exists ONLY in the loading skeleton, so every e2e heading assertion became timing-dependent: asserting before data load silently matches the skeleton, asserting after it fails deterministically. Proven 2026-08-03 by local Playwright run on develop 3af42e29b - a probe asserting the retired heading passed in 152ms before load and failed after load.
